case.display_name: UMG/Sony Music v. Suno AI (D. Mass.) — Motion to Add 61,026 Recordings
case.case_name: Universal Music Group; Sony Music Entertainment; et al. v. Suno, Inc.

coverage.headline: Judge clears UMG and Sony to accuse Suno of pirating YouTube via 'stream ripping' to train its AI
coverage.summary: Judge Saylor cleared UMG and Sony to amend their complaint to allege Suno trained its AI by stream-ripping YouTube, adding DMCA circumvention claims. Fact discovery in the Massachusetts case closes September 30, 2026, with both sides expected to move for summary judgment on the fair-use question.

coverage.headline: Why a fight over 61,000 recordings could shape the future of AI music licensing
coverage.summary: Judge Saylor has yet to rule on the motion to add 61,026 works; Suno opposed the motion on June 4, arguing it would deny the company a timely fair-use ruling. Dispositive motions are due April 9, 2027, and any ruling is expected to reshape licensing leverage across the AI music industry.

coverage.headline: Suno asks court to block UMG and Sony from expanding copyright lawsuit to over 61,000 recordings
coverage.summary: Suno filed its opposition on June 4 to the labels' motion to add 61,026 recordings, arguing the expansion would deny it a timely ruling on whether AI training on copyrighted music constitutes fair use. Suno characterized the motion as a litigation tactic designed to delay and overwhelm the defense.

coverage.headline: UMG and Sony seek to add over 61k recordings to Suno lawsuit after discovery reveals AI trained on 'millions' of their copyrighted tracks
coverage.summary: UMG and Sony filed a motion on May 21 to add 61,026 recordings identified via audio fingerprinting to their D. Mass. complaint, describing that figure as 'only a small fraction' of the matches their experts found. Suno had previously refused to disclose details of its training data, prompting the labels to use Audible Magic fingerprinting technology.
